mustFix.bytesContradicting: Parsed from docs/coop/artifacts/sarif-fc-nonauth-term-golden.v3.review-independent.claude2.json (73b9b58137ebbb710eaaac71048ffd3d0c8d1f7815e7f812c1b4c4d461ea7884, mode 0444, re-verified at review start and at write): OBS-1 keys = [detail, id, note, title, whyNotCharged]; OBS-2 keys = [detail, id, title, whyNotCharged]; OBS-3 = [detail, id, title, whyNotCharged]; OBS-4 = [detail, id, title, whyNotCharged]; OBS-5 = [detail, id, title, whyNotCharged]. Union across the five = [detail, id, note, title, whyNotCharged]; intersection = [detail, id, title, whyNotCharged]; the five member sets are NOT equal. 'note' is present on exactly one of five objects. The stated set is the union, not any object's schema and not the shared schema.
mustFix.whyMustFix: Read the only way COORD's own convention supports, the sentence is false of four of the five frozen objects. The convention is unambiguous and unbroken: of the sixteen '(with members ...)' parentheticals in COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md, all fifteen that describe more than one object read 'each with members ...' (lines 15220, 15337, 15454, 15477, 15569, 15690, 15726, 15804, 15822, 15919, 15998, 16015, 16136, plus 15207 and the D-284 instance), and the only two that drop 'each' describe exactly one object (line 16110 'returned 1 named observations object OBS-1 (with members id, severity, location, note)'; line 16114 'returned 1 unlabeled observationsNotFindings object (with members observation, whyNotAFinding ...)'). The distributive reading is also confirmed against bytes at the nearest precedent: D-284 line 15206-15207 writes '4 named observationsNotFindings objects OBS-1, OBS-2, OBS-3, OBS-4 (each with members id, class, where, text)', and state-class-leftover-join.v4.review-independent.claude2.json carries exactly those four members on all four objects (member sets byte-equal). So the record has never used this parenthetical as a union, and the draft is the first entry to state a member list that no described object combination satisfies. This is not a missing-disclosure defect of the class the predecessors charged as SHOULD-FIX (golden.v1 Codex: a load-bearing provenance edge absent, expressly 'not a fixture-byte or semantic MUST-FIX'; golden.v2 Claude SF-1: ten fields still speaking as the predecessor). It is an affirmative statement about frozen bytes that the frozen bytes refute, entering an append-only record whose only repair is a successor entry. The over-attributed member is also the load-bearing one: 'note' exists on OBS-1 alone and reads 'Reviewer-local label for this review only, following the OBS-n precedent of the golden.v1 Claude review. Not a record identifier.' Attributing it to all five misstates the labels' standing in the same breath the entry names them.

coordinatorSummary: The draft's load-bearing limbs are clean. HEAD, both file digests, the last heading, required-now 28, conditions 2/4/5, the DR-122 status token, the D-056 gate sentences, the D-182 leftover standing, the D-293 Decision 8 warrant, the no-cell-edit branch (correctly extended to D-295, correctly excluding D-236 and CONTESTED D-272), the two namedCases, the platformless fixture directory and both Stage A ACCEPT 0/0 verdicts all verify from the bytes. The three defects are all in the Stage A observation-disposition limb. MF1: the member-list parenthetical states a schema four of the five frozen observation objects do not have, in a record whose own sixteen-instance convention reads that parenthetical distributively. SF1: bare reviewer-local labels are called 'Claude Stage A identifiers' and given a disposition COORD reserves for globally-scoped tokens, contradicting the note member of OBS-1 itself and colliding with the identical tokens minted by the golden.v1 and golden.v2 Claude reviews that this same entry names. SF2: the asymmetry guard that all three matching precedents carry is missing. All three repairs are mechanical, invent no identifier, and touch nothing outside lines 50-57 and the honesty-work sentence at line 65.
